cite_pills.title: What USB power rating do I need to power my Starlink Mini?

turns.answer:
The Starlink Mini can be powered through USB-C, but it requires a USB-C Power Delivery (USB-C PD) source capable of supplying sufficient power at 20V.

Starlink Mini USB-C power requirements

Specification

	

Requirement




USB-C protocol

	

USB Power Delivery (PD)




USB-C voltage

	

20V DC




Recommended charger

	

100W USB-C PD




Recommended current capacity

	

5A at 20V




Typical power consumption

	

25–40W




USB-C cable

	

100W-rated (5A, e-marked) cable




Connector at Starlink Mini

	

Proprietary DC barrel-style power input

Important: The Starlink Mini does not have a native USB-C power input. You need a compatible USB-C-to-Starlink Mini DC power cable that negotiates the correct voltage.

Supported, provided 20V/5A is available

Starlink's current USB-C guidance specifies 100W minimum, even though the Mini normally consumes substantially less power. 
Starlink Help Center
+1

Power bank considerations

For a power bank, check that one USB-C port can deliver 100W at 20V/5A. A power bank advertised as 100W total across multiple ports may not qualify.

At an average 30W load, a 100Wh battery would theoretically last about 3.3 hours, or roughly 2.5–3 hours after conversion losses.

Official references: Starlink Mini power requirements and Starlink Mini USB-C cable specifications.
